core_obligations: Observe that the displayed diagram expressing the sheaf of units via the multiplication map is cartesian (proof lines 8025-8034).
Apply exactness of f^{-1} to conclude that the pulled-back diagram is cartesian, giving f^{-1}(O^*) = (f^{-1}O)^* (proof lines 8035-8050).
Deduce the second statement: if O makes the site locally ringed, then with f^sharp = id the morphism (f, f^sharp) is a morphism of locally ringed topoi.
proof_roadmap: Identify the units by a cartesian diagram.
Pull it back along the exact functor f^{-1}.
Read off the locally ringed conclusion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the pullback of the sheaf of units is the sheaf of units of the pulled-back structure sheaf, and deduces that a morphism of topoi whose structure map is the identity is a morphism of locally ringed topoi whenever the target is locally ringed. The proof observes that the diagram expressing the units as a fibre product over the multiplication map is cartesian, and uses exactness of the pullback functor to conclude that the pulled-back diagram is cartesian as well; the locally ringed conclusion then follows from the locally ringed condition being checked on the pulled-back structure sheaf with identity structure map (proof lines 8024-8050). H2: the cartesianity argument for the unit group sheaf is the substance and is carried out in detail.
